why: The reader reaches this through Holmes's own objection at ¶57: why not injure the horse in the stall? It is answered by what the cut needed. The fine cut needed a light and freedom to work, out of hearing of the lads in the loft above the stable (¶19, ¶34). ¶223 states it: a pricked horse would have roused the soundest sleepers, so it had to be done in the open air.

value: to do something to the horse himself
note: ¶223: a pricked horse would wake the lads in the loft, so the cut had to be done in the open air, away from the stables.

value: to do something to him that could not be done in the stall
note: ¶223: the horse would have roused the soundest sleepers when it felt the knife, so the cut had to be done in the open air.
